Mr. M. Nurullah with Mr. AKM Safiullah, Mr. Shah Miron Alam and Mr. Bazlul Kabir, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner.

parties:
Mir Amir Ali ----- Accused Petitioner.
Vs.
The State ----- Opposite Party.
full_judgment: 13. Mr. S B Barua, the learned Advocate appearing for the State, submits that the accused petitioner exceeded his authority as Accounts Officer of the Upazila as without prior sanction or approval from the Education Officer he sent the bills for payment against the GP Fund to the depositees. The contention of Mr. Barua does not get support from the allegations made in the FIR. There is also no document or paper to show that the Accounts Officer passed the bills without having any authority from the Upazila Education Officer. On the prayer of the learned Advocate for the State, the hearing of the case was twice adjourned so as to enable him to bring the documents and papers if any seized by the investigation officer but the learned Advocate for the State expressed his inability to produce any such document or paper as he did not receive any response from the Deputy Commissioner, Gaibandha in spite of his best effort. In the absence of any paper and document we are to depend entirely on the FIR, the charge sheet and the affidavits. In this case no counter affidavit has been sworn on behalf of the State and the averments made in the application have thus remained unchallenged point raised by Mr. Nurullah is the point of limitation. The learned Advocate also submits that the proceeding cannot be allowed to continue beyond the period of limitation without complying with the provision of section 167(5)(6)(7) CrPC and hence it is liable to be stopped and the accused petitioner is entitled to be released. We are not inclined to take up the point relating to limitation at this stage in the case as we think that the most pertinent question is whether the statement made in the FIR and the charge sheet disclose any prima facie case of criminal misappropriation or criminal breach of trust and for that matter initiation and continuation of the case under section 409 will amount to abuse of the process of Court. As we have already found that there was no allegation of entrustment to and or of misappropriation by the accused petitioner of any money said to have been given to and taken by the depositees from their respective GP Fund Accounts, we are of the view that to allow the criminal case to continue will amount to causing harassment to the accused petitioner particularly in the case which was started in the year 1985 and has still been continuing even after the recovery on repayment of loan by the loanees towards the adjustment of GP Fund Account which fact has not been controverted by anybody from the side of the prosecution.
